1 thereby accused caused wrongful loss to the complainant.
FIR bearing no. 51/21 was registered against him.

After completion of investigation, Charge Sheet (Fi- nal Report, u/s 173 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, in short 'Cr.PC') for commission of offences punishable u/s 420/34 IPC was filed in the court.
2. To bring home the guilt of the accused, prosecution has cited as many as 14 (Fourteen) witnesses.

3. PW-1/complainant in his deposition, failed to identify the accused person and did not support the prosecution story by resiling from his previous statement.
4.

Since the PW1/complainant Ramesh Chand Bist resiled from his previous statement regarding identity of accused person as well as facts of the case, he was cross-examined by learned APP for the State with the leave of the court.
5. The complainant, who is the star witness to the incident, had turned hostile regarding identity of accused person as well as facts of the case.

The prosecution has failed to examine any public witness therefore, the version of the prosecution has SAHIL MONGA State Vs. Imran Page No.2 of 6 FIR No.51/21 remained uncorroborated by any independent material witness.

In this regard reference may be made to a Division Bench judgment of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court passed in the case of Govind & Ors vs.
The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104(2003) DLT 510 wherein it was held that:-
"...In cases where ultimate chance of conviction is very bleak or there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction in such cases no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution and trial to continue.

8. I have heard the learned counsel for the accused and the learned APP for the State and have perused the records very carefully.

It is submitted on behalf of the accused that the complainant has completely turned hostile on the facts of the case and cross-examined by the APP for the State but nothing could be elicited from him which could indicate complicity of the accused in the crime.
Thus, according to him, prosecution has miserably failed to establish the identity of the accused as well as facts of the case beyond reasonable doubt.
10. It is, therefore, prayed that the accused may be acquitted of the charge levelled against him.
Decision and brief reasons for the same 11.

The rule that every accused person is presumed innocent until he is proved guilty and that it is the duty of the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt is fundamental to the system of justice practiced in this country and in several other countries.
Indeed it is entrenched in the Constitution that every person charged with a criminal offence shall be presumed to be innocent until he is proved or has pleaded guilty.
12. Onus is, thus, on the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the person facing the trial is, in fact, the same person who committed the offence.

13. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi while dealing with the identity of the accused in the case of Ashraf vs State held as under:-

Imran Page No.4 of 6 FIR No.51/21 completely hostile with regard to identity of the accused even in his examination-in-chief and nothing could be elicited from him to show the involvement of the accused in the offence in the cross-examination by the APP, such a testimony cannot be accepted and made the basis of the conviction....."
14. It was argued on behalf of the accused that prosecution has failed to prove that accused was the perpetrator of the crime.
PW-1 has completely turned hostile on the facts of the case.

15. Since the witness resiled from his previous statement purportedly given to the police during investigation, he was cross-examined by the learned APP for the State with the permission of the court but nothing incriminating against the accused could be elicited.

16. Rest witnesses are formal in nature and the facts of the case cannot be established from their testimonies, inasmuch as, the alleged incident was neither committed in their presence nor it is the case of the prosecution.
